sections.overview: Apistogramma pertensis is a small freshwater cichlid from Brazil, described by C. T. Haseman in 1911. FishBase calls it the Amazon dwarf cichlid and records it from the lower Rio Negro and the Amazon-Solimões corridor.
sections.identification: Adults are slender, with a dark lateral band and a distinct caudal-base spot; preserved and live color patterns can vary. FishBase lists 3.9 cm standard length for male or unsexed fish and a separate 4.5 cm total-length record for females, so those values are not directly comparable. No reliable mass, width or body-height value was found in the cited species accounts.
sections.habitat: The range includes the lower Rio Negro and reaches along the Amazon-Solimões from near Manacapuru toward Monte Alegre. Species accounts place it in freshwater tropical river systems, but detailed site-by-site habitat measurements are sparse.
sections.diet: No species-specific diet study was located. A French aquarium reference describes small invertebrates as food, a plausible account for a bottom-foraging dwarf cichlid but not a measured stomach-content result.
sections.behavior: The summary documents female care during cave spawning, but it offers no detailed field observations of social behavior outside reproduction.
sections.reproduction: The female attaches about 120 eggs to a cave ceiling and guards the clutch, according to a species account. No population-level range for clutch size is provided.
sections.ecology: Apistogramma pertensis is a close lookalike of A. meinkeni and A. iniridae in the informal pertensis group. A. meinkeni has offset broken caudal bars, while A. iniridae has a lateral stripe that continues onto the caudal peduncle; compare these details before relying on range alone.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN category is Least Concern, with the assessment dated 29 October 2020. This is the latest assessment date shown in FishBase.
